comment: Malformed header text, exercised on BOTH codecs. None of tests/vectors/frames.json is malformed, which is why six hostile inputs found real disagreement between the Java and Python codecs (see plan fix b81e6bc) before this file existed. header_text is the raw header text a peer would place on the wire between the length prefix and the newline -- NOT a full encoded frame. Every case here must be rejected by both Json.parse (Java) and json.loads plus _check_header (Python) when wrapped in a frame. Every case that has a JSON object at all begins with the REQUIRED fields "v":1,"t":"x" and that prefix is load-bearing -- do not strip it as noise. Without it every case carried only the key "a", so _check_header's missing-required-field rule fired first and five cases (integer_beyond_int64, lone_surrogate, nested_object, unpaired_low_surrogate, high_surrogate_not_followed_by_escape) never reached the rule they exist to pin: deleting the unpaired-surrogate check in codec.py outright still left the suite at 179 passed. empty_input and whitespace_only have no object to prefix, and want none -- their intended rule, "this is not JSON at all", already fires first.

cases.name: bare_minus
cases.why: a lone minus with no digits; Java's Long.parseLong would throw NumberFormatException if not guarded

cases.name: integer_beyond_int64
cases.why: 20-digit integer exceeds signed 64-bit range; Java's Long.parseLong throws, Python's unbounded int previously accepted it silently

cases.name: bad_u_hex_escape
cases.why: a \u escape with a non-hex character; Java's Integer.parseInt(hex,16) would throw NumberFormatException if not validated first

cases.name: truncated_u_escape
cases.why: a \u escape cut off before its 4 hex digits are available

cases.name: lone_surrogate
cases.why: an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate from a \u escape; survives naive parsing and corrupts silently on re-encode (Java writes '?', Python raises UnicodeEncodeError)

cases.name: trailing_garbage
cases.why: data after the closing brace of the top-level object; Python's json.loads raises 'Extra data'

cases.name: leading_zeros
cases.why: leading zeros are not valid JSON numbers; Python's json.loads rejects them

cases.name: unterminated_string
cases.why: a string value with no closing quote

cases.name: unterminated_object
cases.why: an object with no closing brace

cases.name: whitespace_only
cases.why: header text that is only whitespace, no object at all

cases.name: nested_object
cases.why: a nested object; the header schema is flat by design and must reject this, not half-parse it

cases.name: unpaired_low_surrogate
cases.why: a low surrogate with no preceding high surrogate; only valid as the second half of a pair

cases.name: high_surrogate_not_followed_by_escape
cases.why: a high surrogate followed by a plain character instead of a \u low-surrogate escape; a supplementary character must be a PAIR of escapes

cases.name: raw_control_char_0x01_in_string
cases.why: a literal 0x01 byte, unescaped, directly inside a JSON string value; RFC 8259 forbids raw control characters in strings -- only the ESCAPED form (\u0001) is legal

cases.name: raw_newline_0x0a_in_string
cases.why: a literal 0x0A (LF) byte, unescaped, directly inside a JSON string value; only the ESCAPED form (\n) is legal JSON
